title: The Harvest Festival
clue: A little autumn fair is opening, and your dog is the judge.
reveal: Set up four tiny harvest stalls and let your dog tour them: a leaf pile, a squash stand behind a gate, a cozy sack and a water bowl. The stall they linger at longest wins the festival prize, a toy waiting in the winner's spot.
objective: Let your dog tour four tiny autumn stalls and see which one they choose.
instructions: Choose a yard, garage or room corner. Check the area for fungus, mushrooms, fallen apples or corn cobs and clear them. Wet leaves are slippery.

Build the stalls: a shallow box of dry, clean leaves you checked today for mold and mushrooms, a small whole pumpkin or squash on a mat behind a baby gate or chair barrier, a cloth sack or towel nest, and a bowl of fresh water.
Hide a favorite toy in the leaf pile. The squash and any decorative gourds are for looking and sniffing through the barrier only, never within reach of teeth.
Walk your dog through the festival on a slack leash or let them wander in. They can sniff, play or skip any stall.
Watch which stall holds their interest longest and say nothing. That is the winner of the festival.
Give the festival prize: a toy or quiet time at the winning stall, with a fresh bowl of water.
Tidy the leaves and squash away afterwards so nothing is chewed unseen.
twist: Your dog is the festival judge: the stall they choose wins, and the prize goes there.
variations: Slow version: set up only two stalls, the leaf pile and the sack, for a dog who likes things calm.
Indoor version: use a laundry basket of clean towels instead of leaves.
For a puppy: one stall and one toy, two minutes.
Food-free by design; no tasting needed.
completion: Your dog has toured the stalls and you know their favorite.
photoIdea: Your dog at the winning stall, relaxed and natural, taken from a distance.
safety: Keep pumpkins, gourds, corn cobs, apple cores, grapes and raisins out of reach; they are not dog snacks.
Check leaves for fungus, mushrooms and mold before use; wet leaves are slippery.
Supervise the whole festival, and tidy leaves and squash away afterward so nothing is chewed unseen.
